/.description: A desktop app that turns folders into websites.
/.preview: A desktop app that turns your folder of markdown files into a website. Right-click → your site is live.
/.title: moss

/docs/.description: Learn how to use moss to turn folders into websites.
/docs/.preview: Right-click any folder in Finder and choose Publish with moss. If the folder has markdown files, you already have a website. If it's empty, moss opens the editor so you can create your first page.
/docs/.title: Documentation

/docs/author/.description: Shape your pages with frontmatter and shortcodes.
/docs/author/.preview: Once your folder is a site, the next step is shaping how each page looks and connects to others.
/docs/author/.title: Author

/docs/author/frontmatter/.description: Metadata fields that control how moss treats each page.
/docs/author/frontmatter/.preview: Frontmatter is a block of YAML at the very top of a markdown file, between two --- lines. It tells moss about the page — its title, date, visibility, and more.
/docs/author/frontmatter/.title: Frontmatter

/docs/author/links/.description: Wikilinks, embeds, cross-references, and bilingual content.
/docs/author/links/.preview: Link to any page in your site using double brackets:
/docs/author/links/.title: Links & Embeds

/docs/author/shortcodes/.description: Layout blocks and components that extend markdown.
/docs/author/shortcodes/.preview: Shortcodes are special blocks in your markdown that create layouts and components beyond what standard markdown offers — grids, galleries, hero images, and more. They use ::: block syntax.
/docs/author/shortcodes/.title: Shortcodes

/docs/deploy/.description: Publish your site to GitHub Pages.
/docs/deploy/.preview: - A GitHub account - A GitHub repository (public or private)
/docs/deploy/.title: Deploy

/docs/design/.description: Make it yours with CSS and JavaScript.
/docs/design/.title: Design

/docs/design/css/.description: CSS variables, dark mode, and component class names.
/docs/design/css/.preview: Create style.css in your project root. moss loads it after the default theme, so your rules override the defaults.
/docs/design/css/.title: CSS

/docs/design/javascript/.description: Custom scripts, data attributes, and DOM structure.
/docs/design/javascript/.preview: Create script.js in your project root. moss loads it after all built-in scripts, so the DOM is ready when your code runs.
/docs/design/javascript/.title: JavaScript

/docs/extend/.description: Build plugins that hook into the build pipeline.
/docs/extend/.preview: Plugins are JavaScript bundles in .moss/plugins/{name}/. They attach to five stages of the build pipeline — transforming content, injecting into template slots, deploying, or syndicating.
/docs/extend/.title: Extend

/docs/extend/cli/.description: Command-line interface for testing and automation.
/docs/extend/cli/.preview: | Command | Description | |---------|-------------| | moss preview | Open folder in preview with file watching and hot reload | | moss compile | Compile folder to static site (output in .moss/site/) | | moss compile --serve | Compile and start a local HTTP server | | moss compile --watch | Compile...
/docs/extend/cli/.title: CLI

/docs/extend/hooks/.description: The plugin lifecycle — five capabilities and their contexts.
/docs/extend/hooks/.preview: When moss compiles a site, it runs through these stages in order:
/docs/extend/hooks/.title: Hooks

/docs/extend/manifest/.description: Plugin manifest reference, configuration, and the moss-api SDK.
/docs/extend/manifest/.preview: .moss/plugins/my-plugin/ ├── manifest.json Plugin metadata and config ├── main.bundle.js Built JavaScript entry point ├── config.json Runtime config (overrides defaults) └── icon.svg Plugin icon (optional)
/docs/extend/manifest/.title: Manifest

/docs/extend/slots/.description: Template injection points and the enhance phase.
/docs/extend/slots/.preview: Slots are named injection points in the HTML template where plugins can insert content. There are six slots:
/docs/extend/slots/.title: Slots

/docs/media/.description: Images, video, notebooks, and other files in your site.
/docs/media/.preview: Put images, videos, and other files anywhere in your project folder. Reference them from markdown and moss handles the rest — path resolution, optimization, and progressive loading.
/docs/media/.title: Media

/docs/structure/.description: How files and folders become pages, sections, and navigation.
/docs/structure/.preview: Every .md file in your folder becomes a page. Every subfolder becomes a section.
